newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks continue active and firmer.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks continue active and firmer.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks continued firm in active trade on Monday with many investors abandoning the local money market where interest rates were low in favour of the equity market, brokers said.

"If inflation doesn't get out of hand and go beyond the 20s we should continue to see a lot of movement to the equity as opposed to the local money market and other forms of investment," one dealer said.
"Investors are holding on to their scrip and that's pushing the shares even further up. There's actually a shortage of scrip at the moment," he added.

On Monday, the key 57-counter industrial index put on 61.22 points to close at 10,174.02, buyoed by gains in food processer Cairns, which surged 250 cents to 1,900, tobacco firm Rothmans which added 200 cents to 6,200, and bankers Barclays, 100 cents firmer at 3,500. Other counters to advance were TSL, another tobacco company, which put on 25 cents to 800, while paper and packaging group Hunyani Warrants at 165 and retailers and hoteliers Meikles at 2,015 were both 15 cents stronger.

On the losing side were tobacco processors BAT which shed 200 cents to 2,100, wire and cable firm Bicaf which eased 20 cents to 400 while battery makers Chloride lost 10 cents to 130 and discount house DCZ were five cents down at 240.

Minings continued lifeless, largely on the back of poor international gold prices with most counters trading unchanged while nickel producer Bindura added 10 cents to 860, and coal giant Wankie shed 25 cents to 450. The seven-share mining index lost 5.93 points to 1048.56.
